author: Shabiha Akter
title: Draymond Green Fires Back at Stephen A. Smith Over Media Accountability Debate on Luka Doncic Trade - NewsBreak
text:
By Shabiha Akter ,
47 minutes ago
Draymond Green and Stephen A. Smith (Photo By Imagn Images) Luka Doncic’s blockbuster trade last season quickly became one of the most controversial moves in recent NBA history. Even Golden State Warriors veteran Draymond Green admitted that the move proved that anything can happen in today’s NBA .
Former Dallas Mavericks general manager Nico Harrison was the key figure behind the trade decision. While Harrison faced widespread criticism after the move, Green recently made headlines for publicly supporting him. The Warriors forward argued that Harrison had been treated unfairly by the media. However, his comments drew strong pushback from ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith.
In a recent episode of his podcast, Green addressed the criticism and pushed back against Smith while discussing the broader issue of accountability in sports media coverage of the Doncic trade.
“ The problem that I have is we’re calling for all this accountability, but all these guys just get to say things and there’s zero accountability. There’s zero accountability when it comes to me. Just literally get to throw sh*t at a wall and see if it sticks. Zero accountability. But always want to hold others accountable ,” Green said.
“I don’t understand. Like these guys don’t have to answer for these awful a** takes they make. How wrong they be in most situations. But these are experts. I don’t understand it. It’s the only thing you can become an expert in and never have any experience with the game.”
Meanwhile, Harrison ultimately faced consequences for the controversial decision. The Mavericks organization dismissed him from his role as general manager earlier this season after growing frustration from the fanbase. The trade itself also failed to produce the results Dallas had hoped for.
In the deal, the Mavericks acquired Anthony Davis in exchange for Luka Doncic. However, Davis struggled to make an impact during his brief time with the team due to limited availability. Eventually, during this February’s trade deadline, Dallas traded him to the Washington Wizards .
Warriors Reportedly Want Draymond Green to Finish Career with the Franchise Draymond Green (Image Credits: Imagn) Interestingly, during this year’s February trade deadline, Green himself became the subject of speculation regarding his future with the Warriors . However, once the deadline passed, Green remained in the Golden State. Tim Kawakami recently reported that Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. publicly reaffirmed the organization’s commitment to the longtime star.
“ We want Draymond here, we want him to finish his career here, just like we do Steph ,” Kawakami reported.
While his career has occasionally been overshadowed by on-court controversies and heated moments, Green’s impact on the franchise remains undeniable. He has now spent 14 seasons in the NBA since being selected in the 2012 draft, and every one of those seasons has been with the Warriors. Throughout that time, he has played a crucial role in Golden State’s dynasty by helping the team capture four NBA championships.
